target_model_responses.dim2_response:
**One‑Week Home‑Cooking Meal Plan**  
*Designed for a user who likes to control ingredients, with easy‑prep “make‑once‑eat‑twice” dishes that cover dinner and next‑day lunch.*

---

## 1. Overview & Core Templates
The plan re‑uses the four **meal‑planning templates** described in the weekly guide [[summaries/session-01_2024-06-15]]:

| Template | Typical Protein | Main Veggies | Base / Sauce |
|----------|----------------|--------------|--------------|
| **Stir‑fry** | Chicken thighs **or** tofu | Bell peppers, broccoli | Soy‑ginger sauce |
| **One‑pan roasted** | Chicken thighs | Potatoes, carrots or green beans | Olive‑oil, herbs |
| **Tomato‑basil pasta** | (optional) chicken breast | Spinach | Marinara sauce, fresh basil |
| **Bean‑and‑grain bowl** | Black beans (canned) | Roasted veg, spinach | Yogurt‑lime dressing |

These templates are already tuned for 3‑serving portions, a 60‑90 min Sunday prep workflow, and container sizing [[summaries/session-01_2024-06-15]].

---

## 2. Daily Schedule (Dinner → Next‑Day Lunch)

| Day | Dinner | Next‑Day Lunch (leftover) |
|-----|--------|---------------------------|
| **Mon** | Chicken (or tofu) stir‑fry | Leftover stir‑fry |
| **Tue** | One‑pan roasted chicken thighs + potatoes (plus carrots/green beans) | Re‑heat roasted chicken & veg (or chop for a cold salad) |
| **Wed** | Tomato‑basil pasta with spinach | Leftover pasta |
| **Thu** | Bean‑and‑grain bowl (rice/quinoa, black beans, roasted veg, yogurt‑lime dressing) | Bowl rebuilt from remaining grains/beans/veg |
| **Fri** | **Flex day** – use any leftover bowl ingredients or make a quick **egg‑or‑tofu scramble** with any veg that’s still fresh |
| **Sat** | **Veggie‑focused stir‑fry** – use the remaining bell‑pepper & broccoli mix with extra tofu (or a second batch of chicken breast if you like) | Leftover scramble or stir‑fry |
| **Sun** | **Simple sheet‑pan salmon (or optional plant‑based protein)** with **roasted potatoes & carrots** (use any veg left) | Light salad using any leftover spinach, basil, and a drizzle of olive oil |

*(If you don’t eat fish, replace the salmon with extra tofu or a second serving of the chicken‑thigh stir‑fry.)*

---

## 3. Shopping List (exact amounts for 1‑2 people, 3‑serving portions)

| Item | Quantity | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| Chicken thighs | **1 ½ lb** (≈ 680 g) | For stir‑fry & roasted pan |
| Chicken breast **or** tofu | **½ lb chicken** **or** **14‑16 oz tofu** | Stir‑fry protein option |
| Bell peppers | **3–4** (mixed colors) | Slice for stir‑fry & weekend |
| Broccoli | **1 head** | Florets for stir‑fry |
| Potatoes | **1 lb** (≈ 450 g) | Roast & sheet‑pan |
| Carrots **or** green beans | **½ lb** | Roast & weekend |
| Fresh spinach | **5–6 oz** | Pasta & bowls |
| Fresh basil | **1 small bunch** | Pasta & garnish |
| Marinara sauce (jar, ~24 oz) | **1 jar** | Pasta |
| Black beans (canned, 15 oz) | **1 can** | Bowl |
| Dry pasta | **8 oz** | Spaghetti or penne |
| Rice‑quinoa blend (dry) | **1½ cups** (≈ 300 g) | Bowls |
| Limes or lemons | **2–3** | Dressing |
| Garlic | **1 head** | Minced for sauces |
| Soy sauce | **a few tbsp** | Stir‑fry sauce |
| Olive oil | **a few tbsp** | Roasting & dressings |
| Optional protein for Sunday | **1 fillet salmon (≈ 6‑8 oz)** or extra tofu | Sheet‑pan dinner |
| Eggs (if using scramble) | **4‑6** | Fri/Sat scramble |
| Yogurt (plain) | **½ cup** | Yogurt‑lime dressing |

*(All items are taken directly from the grocery list in the weekly guide [[summaries/session-01_2024-06-15]])*

---

## 4. Sunday (or “Prep Day”) Workflow – 60 – 90 min  

Follow the **food‑prep workflow** from the source [[summaries/session-01_2024-06-15]]:

1. **Cook the grain** – Rinse 1½ cups rice‑quinoa, cook in a pot (2 : 1 water), cool, store in a 32‑oz container.  
2. **Prep vegetables** – Slice bell peppers, cut broccoli into florets; store together in a 32‑oz container.  
3. **Carrots/green beans** – Chop to bite‑size, store in a 16‑oz container.  
4. **Spinach & basil** – Store spinach in a 16‑oz container with a paper towel; basil in an 8‑oz container, lightly damp.  
5. **Proteins** – Dice the chicken breast or tofu (≈ 10‑12 oz) and place in a 16‑oz container; season the chicken thighs and keep in a separate 16‑oz container.  
6. **Sauces** – Mix a simple **soy‑ginger sauce** (2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, a splash water) in an 8‑oz jar. Prepare **yogurt‑lime dressing** (½ cup plain yogurt, juice of 1 lime, pinch salt) in another 8‑oz jar. Label both.  
7. **Roast veg** – Toss 2 cups mixed veg (half of the bell‑pepper, broccoli, carrots/green beans) with olive oil, salt, pepper; roast 425 °F for 20 min, cool, store in a 16‑oz container.  
8. **Garlic** – Mince 2 cloves, store in a 4‑oz container (good for sauces).  

> **Container sizing** follows the guidelines in the plan (grain → 32 oz, veg → 32 oz, proteins → 16 oz, sauces → 8 oz, etc.) [[summaries/session-01_2024-06-15]].

---

## 5. Daily Cooking Steps (Quick Reference)

| Day | Main Action | Time Needed |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| **Mon** – Stir‑fry | Heat 1 tbsp olive oil, add garlic, protein, veg, pour soy‑ginger sauce, stir 5‑7 min. | 15 min |
| **Tue** – One‑pan roast | Toss chicken thighs, potatoes, carrots with olive oil, salt, pepper; bake 425 °F 25‑30 min (flip halfway). | 30 min |
| **Wed** – Pasta | Cook pasta (8 min), heat marinara, toss with spinach until wilted, add basil. | 15 min |
| **Thu** – Bean‑&‑grain bowl | Re‑heat rice‑quinoa, black beans, roasted veg; drizzle yogurt‑lime dressing, top with fresh spinach. | 10 min |
| **Fri** – Flex | Use any leftover grains/beans/veg; optionally scramble 2‑3 eggs with veg. | 10‑15 min |
| **Sat** – Veggie stir‑fry | Same as Mon, but use remaining veg & tofu (or extra chicken). | 15 min |
| **Sun** – Sheet‑pan | Arrange salmon (or tofu) + remaining potatoes + carrots on pan, drizzle olive oil, roast 400 °F 20‑25 min. | 30 min |

All meals stay under 30 minutes once prep is done, letting you keep tight control over salts, oils, and additives.

---

## 6. Storage & Reuse Tips

* **Grains** keep 4‑5 days in the 32‑oz container.  
* **Stir‑fry veg** stay 3‑4 days; keep sauces separate to avoid sogginess.  
* **Roasted veg** last 4‑5 days; can be eaten cold in salads.  
* **Raw chicken/tofu** should be used within 2 days (store in their 16‑oz containers).  
* **Sauces & garlic** stay 3‑5 days refrigerated.  

These storage guidelines are taken from the **container‑sizing** section of the weekly guide [[summaries/session-01_2024-06-15]].

---

### TL;DR

1. **Shop** using the exact list above.  
2. **Prep** everything on Sunday following the 60‑90 min workflow.  
3. **Cook** the four core templates (stir‑fry, roasted chicken, pasta, bean‑bowl) for Mon‑Thu; reuse leftovers for next‑day lunches.  
4. **Flex** Friday‑Sunday with quick scramble, extra stir‑fry, or sheet‑pan salmon using any remaining ingredients.  

This schedule gives you complete ingredient control, minimal daily cooking time, and balanced nutrition throughout the week. Enjoy!

**How to pick a quick, balanced dinner while you’re staying somewhere with limited options**

1. **Survey what’s on hand** – Look at the hotel lobby shop, mini‑fridge, or any nearby convenience store. Typical grab‑and‑go items are listed in the **[[concepts/grab-and-go-meal-combinations]]** concept (e.g., pre‑cooked chicken strips, tuna packets, instant oatmeal, crackers, mixed nuts, fruit, baby‑carrots, hummus, yogurt).

2. **Apply the “protein‑first” rule** – Choose one clear protein source first. This keeps you full and preserves muscle mass, a core principle of **[[concepts/healthy-travel-eating]]**.  
   *Examples*: [[entities/rotisserie-chicken-snack-pack]], [[entities/grilled‑chicken‑strips]], [[entities/tuna‑packet]], [[entities/cottage‑cheese]], [[entities/yogurt]], [[entities/protein‑bar]].

3. **Add a carbohydrate or grain** – Pick something that needs little or no preparation.  
   *Examples*: [[entities/rice‑quinoa]] (microwaveable cup), [[entities/instant‑oatmeal]], [[entities/crackers]].

4. **Include a healthy‑fat component** – This smooths blood‑sugar response and adds satiety.  
   *Examples*: [[entities/peanut‑butter]], [[entities/mixed‑nuts]], a drizzle of [[entities/olive‑oil]] (if you have a microwave‑safe dish).

5. **Finish with a fruit or vegetable** – Boost fiber, vitamins, and freshness.  
   *Examples*: [[entities/apple]], [[entities/banana]], [[entities/baby‑carrots]], [[entities/bell‑peppers]], [[entities/broccoli]].

6. **Match to your preferences & constraints**  
   *Time*: If you have <5 min, go for a **no‑microwave** combo (e.g., Yogurt + mixed nuts + apple).  
   *Microwave available*: Use a quick‑cook grain cup (rice/quinoa) and add a protein packet.  
   *Want warm food*: Pick a microwaveable soup/ramen bowl and pair it with a protein bar (**combo 3** in the concept).

7. **Sample quick‑prep combos** (all drawn from the eight practical pairings in **[[concepts/grab-and-go-meal-combinations]]**):

   | Combo | Prep time | Why it works |
   |------|-----------|--------------|
   | **Yogurt + mixed nuts + apple** | 0 min (just open) | Protein + fat + carb/fiber; no fridge needed if yogurt is pre‑chilled. |
   | **Microwaveable rice cup + tuna packet + baby carrots** | 2 min (microwave rice) | Balanced macros; veg adds crunch and micronutrients. |
   | **Instant oatmeal + peanut butter + banana** | 1 min (mix) | Warm carb base, healthy fat, fruit sweetness; good for cooler evenings. |
   | **Hummus + crackers + grilled‑chicken‑strips + bell‑pepper sticks** | 1–2 min (assemble) | Full‑meal feel, protein‑first, veg for volume. |
   | **Rotisserie‑style chicken snack pack + whole‑grain crackers + apple** | 0 min | Simple, portable, satisfies hunger quickly. |

8. **Check any dietary priorities** – If you aim for higher protein, lean toward combos with two protein items (e.g., chicken strips + cottage cheese). If you’re watching carbs, choose nuts, cheese, and a low‑glycemic fruit instead of a grain cup.

9. **Finalize** – Pick the combo that matches your time budget, available equipment, and taste cravings. Write it down or snap a quick photo of the items, then enjoy a balanced dinner without the hassle of cooking.

**Bottom line:**  
1️⃣ Identify a protein → 2️⃣ Add a carb/grain → 3️⃣ Add a healthy fat → 4️⃣ Add fruit/veg → 5️⃣ Adjust for time and taste. This quick decision‑tree aligns with the travel‑eating priorities you’ve followed in previous sessions.
